title: Soft-reserve routing with warm-pools and quota-smoothing for tiered plans
creator: Maya Chen
body:
Background:
Redwood currently enforces strict per-plan admission with abrupt demotions when credits are exhausted. This leads to poor UX for paid customers during short bursts and under-utilized capacity in regions where enterprise usage is low. We need a policy that preserves SLA guarantees for Enterprise and Paid plans while allowing short-term elasticity and maintaining fairness across tenants and regions.

Proposal (high-level):
1) Soft-reserve: reserve a configurable fraction of capacity for Enterprise and Paid lanes (e.g., 30% for Enterprise, 20% for Paid) but allow borrowing from reserves when overall cluster utilization is below a safety threshold. Borrowing creates a debt entry for the tenant’s plan that decays over time (quota-smoothing).

2) Warm-pools: maintain a small warm pool of instances (GPU-ready runtime slices) pre-initialized to hot models for Paid and Enterprise in major regions. Warm pools reduce cold-start latency for bursty paid requests and are tagged with priority lanes to allow faster admission. Warm-pool sizing is autoscaled based on rolling-window burstiness metrics.

3) Quota-smoothing: when a paid tenant borrows reserved capacity, record a debt token balance decayed by an exponential half-life (configurable per plan). Admission controller factors this debt into future soft-reserve allowances so repeated borrowing reduces priority gradually rather than instantly demoting to free lane.

4) Regional spillover and fairness: allow spillover to adjacent regions with a cost multiplier and different decay windows. Prioritize routing that minimizes added latency but falls back to lower-cost regions only when it preserves enterprise SLOs. Implement a per-region fairness score to prevent one tenant from monopolizing warm-pool bursts.

Technical design details:
- Admission controller changes: introduce SoftReservePolicy and WarmPoolAllocator modules. SoftReservePolicy keeps an in-memory sliding window of per-plan utilization, debt ledger (per-tenant), and safety thresholds. WarmPoolAllocator manages warm instance lifecycle and labels nodes with lane tags.
- Debt ledger schema: tenant_id | plan_tier | debt_score | last_updated (we store in our existing token-metrics Redis namespace with TTLs to avoid retention bloat). debt_score is a float represented as a string in the ledger to satisfy metric exporters.
- Router heuristics: when a request arrives, evaluate lane eligibility in this order: reserved-capacity available && debt_score below threshold -> route to reserved lane; else if warm-pool instance available in region -> route to warm instance; else evaluate cross-region spillover if latency penalty < configured threshold; finally, route to free lane variant.
- Safety fallback: if reserved lanes fall below emergency margin, trigger fallback to canary model variant or queue with early rejection headers to clients.

Metrics and SLOs to track:
- p50/p90 latency for each lane (free/paid/enterprise)
- warm-pool hit rate (target 75% for paid during bursts)
- debt_score distribution per tier
- fairness metric: Gini coefficient across tenants within a region for warm-pool consumption
- cost delta (tokens and infra) pre/post rollout

Rollout plan:
1) Simulation: run admission logic in offline mode against historical traces (2 weeks) to tune reserve fractions, half-life of decay, and warm-pool size.
2) Shadow: enable decision logging and route decisions only for 10% of traffic (no effect) for 1 week.
3) Canary: enable soft-reserve and warm-pools in us-west-2 for Paid + Enterprise customers (5% of seats), monitor metrics for 2 weeks.
4) Gradual global rollout with staged increases and automated rollback triggers if warm-pool hit rate drops or latency regresses >10% p90.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for debt decay math and policy thresholds.
- Integration test with local router and fake warm-pool instances.
- Chaos test: simulate sudden credit drain and region outage to verify spillover and fallback.

Operational runbooks:
- Emergency rollback: set soft_reserve_mode=disabled across control plane to revert to strict per-plan admission.
- Observability: add dashboards (Console) showing per-lane latency/cost and per-tenant debt exposures; add alerts when warm-pool utilization >95% or fairness Gini >0.45.

Security and compliance notes:
- Debt ledger contains tenant identifiers; ensure encryption at rest and RBACed access. Audit logging enabled for warm-pool allocation changes.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should decay be for enterprise vs. paid? Enterprise could have slower decay to preserve SLA privileges, paid should decay faster to avoid long-term spike advantage.
- Warm-pool cost vs. benefit: small warm pools reduce latency but increase infra baseline. We need concrete cost models from finance.
- Region choice heuristics: should we prefer lower-cost regions even if latency is slightly worse? (tunable policy)

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Soft-Reserve+Warm-Pools
- Simulation traces & notebooks: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/simulation-2026
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4211

Next steps:
- Complete offline simulation and post results in the design doc (owner: Arjun) — target 2026-02-20.
- Implement debt ledger persistence and unit tests (owner: Priya Rao).
- Prepare console dashboard mockups for PM review (owner: Lina Gomez).
